terms.def: A confidence interval for the difference of two population proportions, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_1 - p_2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>±</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2) \pm z^* \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1(1-\hat{p}_1)}{n_1} + \frac{\hat{p}_2(1-\hat{p}_2)}{n_2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. It needs two independent random samples (or two randomly assigned groups) and at least 10 successes and 10 failures in each.
terms.topicTitle: Constructing a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions

terms.def: The test statistic of a two-sample z test for proportions: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2}{\sqrt{p_c(1 - p_c)\left(\frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_2}\right)}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the observed difference measured in standard errors from 0. The denominator is the standard error built from the pooled proportion <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_c</annotation></semantics></math>.
terms.topicTitle: Carrying Out a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions

terms.def: A significance test of <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_0: p_1 - p_2 = 0</annotation></semantics></math> about two population proportions, using two independent random samples or two randomly assigned groups. Its standard error uses the pooled proportion <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_c</annotation></semantics></math>.
terms.topicTitle: Setting Up a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions

terms.def: A table of counts for two categorical variables: the categories of one variable label the rows, the other the columns, and each cell counts the individuals in that pairing of categories, with row and column totals.
terms.topicTitle: Tabular and Graphical Representations for the Distributions of Two Categorical Variables

terms.def: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true: finding convincing evidence for an effect that is not there. Its probability is the significance level <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.
terms.topicTitle: Potential Errors When Performing Tests

terms.def: Failing to reject the null hypothesis when the alternative is true: missing an effect that is there. Its probability, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, depends on the true value of the parameter.
terms.topicTitle: Potential Errors When Performing Tests

terms.def: An estimator whose sampling distribution is centered at the parameter it estimates, so it is right on average over many samples. A biased estimator's sampling distribution is centered too high or too low.
terms.topicTitle: Estimators

terms.def: Undercoverage happens when part of the population is left out of the sampling frame, so those individuals have no chance of being chosen.
terms.topicTitle: Potential Problems with Sampling

terms.def: A distribution in which all values occur about equally often, so its histogram has bars of about the same height.
terms.topicTitle: Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions

terms.def: The number of peaks (modes) in a distribution: unimodal has one, bimodal has two, multimodal has more.
terms.topicTitle: Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions

terms.def: The union of A and B, written <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∪</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A \cup B</annotation></semantics></math>, is the event that A or B or both happen. The general addition rule gives its probability: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>∪</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(A \cup B)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)</annotation></semantics></math>.
terms.topicTitle: Independent Events and Unions of Events

terms.def: Variability: how far apart the values of a distribution are from each other, or how much they vary.
terms.topicTitle: Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions

terms.def: A characteristic recorded for each observational unit, whose value can differ from one unit to another.
terms.topicTitle: Variables

terms.def: The square of the standard deviation, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}</annotation></semantics></math> for a sample.
terms.topicTitle: Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable

terms.def: A Venn diagram draws the sample space as a rectangle and events as circles inside it. Overlapping circles show outcomes in both events; the regions can hold counts or probabilities.
terms.topicTitle: Independent Events and Unions of Events

terms.def: A voluntary response sample is made of people who choose themselves, for example by answering an online poll. It overrepresents people with strong opinions.
terms.topicTitle: Potential Problems with Sampling

terms.def: Sampling without replacement means an individual can be chosen once; with replacement, an individual is returned and can be chosen again.
terms.topicTitle: Random Sampling

terms.def: The y-intercept of a line <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = a + bx</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, the value of y when <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
terms.topicTitle: Lines: Slope and Intercept

terms.def: The number of standard deviations a value is above or below the mean: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mi>s</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{s}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mi>σ</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> for a population). Positive is above the mean, negative below; it has no units.
terms.topicTitle: Comparisons of the Distributions for One Quantitative Variable

terms.def: The value <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_1 - p_2 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which means the two population proportions are equal. If a confidence interval for <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_1 - p_2</annotation></semantics></math> contains 0, a difference of zero is plausible and there is not convincing evidence of a difference; if 0 is outside the interval, there is.
terms.topicTitle: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Proportions
